statement: UNESCO's Royal Palaces of Abomey designation describes seventeenth-to-nineteenth-century Aja-Fon royal compounds with respected sacred spaces, royal-spirit huts, ancestral tombs and periodic traditional ceremonies; this is evidence for a specific royal ritual landscape, not a founding date for Fon Vodun.

sources.citation: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, 'Royal Palaces of Abomey' (World Heritage 323), sections on authenticity and integrity, https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/323
sources.author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre / Benin heritage authorities
sources.access_note: Full site description read, including 1625–1900 royal timeline, sacred royal sites, ceremonies and traditional family stewardship. No inference that all Fon Vodun rites or deities were represented there.

does_not_demonstrate: Royal palaces dating from 1625 does not date the first appearance of Vodun.
Palace-specific rites must not be generalized to every Aja-Fon community.
Heritage protection and modern rituals do not establish an unchanged historical practice.
adversarial_counter: Royal state ceremony reflects one politically situated part of a wider dynamic set of Fon religious traditions.
notes: Institutional-source audit. Scope: named public page and its content only; no tradition founding-year inference. Independent historical / community review required before status change.
